# BlueTeam.News
### Threat Landscape Briefing · October 21, 2026 · Wednesday

## BLUF
PHP emergency patches address unauthenticated code execution across web-serving runtimes, including embedded installations. Start inventory, patching and compromise review this shift; isolate affected services when updates cannot proceed. Exploitation reporting remains mixed, while PAN-OS ransomware activity and ConnectWise application-identity abuse independently require exposure checks and investigation—not patch verification alone.

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — SHIFT DECISIONS

- **Threat:** PHP fixes lead because the vulnerable runtime can sit beneath otherwise updated applications. PAN-OS requires patch-and-investigate work; ConnectWise requires application containment and tenant persistence review.
- **Exposure:** Local deployment is unknown. Check web-serving PHP, GlobalProtect portals and gateways, and ConnectWise Cloud Backup application identities, including provider-managed services; vendor-side containment does not establish tenant safety.
- **Required decisions:** Application security — identify PHP exposure this shift and patch or isolate affected services — recommended target October 22, 2026; Incident response — preserve PHP evidence this shift and deliver initial compromise findings — recommended target October 23, 2026; Infrastructure — verify CVE-2026-0257 applicability this shift and remediate affected GlobalProtect deployments — recommended target October 22, 2026; Incident response — preserve GlobalProtect evidence this shift and investigate successful suspicious sessions — recommended target October 23, 2026; Identity security — verify ConnectWise applications this shift and keep affected connections disabled — recommended target October 21, 2026; Incident response — investigate affected tenants and identify persistent access — recommended target October 23, 2026; SaaS operations — prepare conditional ConnectWise reconnection readiness — recommended target October 23, 2026.

---

## KEY JUDGMENTS

### Signal 1 — [Horizon 1] PHP runtime fixes require immediate exposure reduction
**Assessment:** Emergency PHP updates address unauthenticated remote code execution in web-serving installations, including software that bundles PHP. Prioritize internet-facing services and isolate affected systems when patching is blocked. Reports establish attack traffic, but do not provide a consistent picture of successful exploitation.

**Confidence:** High — government advisories establish affected scope and fixes; vendor observations differ on exploitation success and visibility.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect PHP installations serving web requests. Fixed branches are `8.5.12`, `8.4.27`, `8.3.36` and `8.2.35`; older branches require supported upgrades or verified distributor backports. CISA reported no observed exploitation at publication, while Cloudflare reported attack traffic and Krebs reported exploitation observations. These statements do not establish equivalent visibility or successful compromise rates. [CISA Advisories, 2026-10-21](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/21/critical-vulnerabilities-php-require-immediate-patching), [CCCS, 2026-10-21](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/al26-026-critical-vulnerabilities-impacting-php-cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619), [Cloudflare Security, 2026-10-21](https://blog.cloudflare.com/php-vulnerabilities-waf-protection/), [Krebs on Security, 2026-10-21](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/10/widespread-php-flaw-may-cause-many-site-outages-today/).

**Defender impact:** Application updates alone do not repair the runtime; inventory must include hosting providers, containers and appliances, while investigation needs web-server process and outbound-connection telemetry.

**Recommended actions:**

- **Act now:** Application security — identify web-serving PHP this shift, including bundled and hosted instances; patch affected runtimes or isolate services until fixed. **Dependencies:** application owners and hosting vendors. **Completion criterion:** record running-version or backport evidence, service tests and containment for blocked updates; escalate unknown ownership — recommended target October 22, 2026.
- Incident response — preserve available web, application, authentication and endpoint evidence this shift; review PHP workers spawning shells, downloading tools or creating unexpected files. **Completion criterion:** initial findings and retention gaps, using deployment/exposure history for lookback rather than disclosure as an earliest-compromise boundary — recommended target October 23, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** Find the PHP runtime beneath the application, and keep affected services isolated when an update cannot proceed.

### Signal 2 — [Horizon 1] GlobalProtect ransomware intrusions reach virtualization infrastructure
**Assessment:** Unit 42 reports continuing ransomware exploitation of vulnerable PAN-OS GlobalProtect portals and gateways, with a documented pivot toward virtualization management. If deployed, verify remediation and review prior VPN access; patching cannot resolve an established foothold.

**Confidence:** High — direct vendor incident-response reporting supports exploitation and the observed pivot; local exposure and campaign victim totals remain unknown.

**What happened:** Unit 42’s October 20 report says its October 19 update continued to observe attempted exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 by Qilin and Inc operators. The authentication bypass permits unauthorized VPN connections. Investigations include a case involving movement to vCenter and guidance to hunt report indicators and activate incident response for associated successful gateway connections. CVE-2026-0257 is KEV-listed; CISA FCEB remediation due June 1, 2026. [Unit 42, 2026-10-20](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/), [CISA KEV catalog, date unavailable](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

**Defender impact:** VPN session logs must connect to internal authentication and virtualization-management activity; endpoint-only review can miss activity outside guest systems.

**Relevance:** Direct match to ransomware and MFA-bypass interests; PAN-OS deployment and affected configuration remain unknown.

**Recommended actions:**

- **Act now:** Infrastructure — verify CVE-2026-0257 applicability and portal/gateway exposure this shift; retrieve vendor guidance through the cited report and apply supported fixes or mitigations. Check management-interface exposure separately. **Completion criterion:** per-appliance versions, tested restrictions and recorded containment for deferred changes — recommended target October 22, 2026.
- Incident response — preserve VPN and management logs this shift; retrieve and validate indicators from the cited Unit 42 report, investigate associated successful gateway connections and trace internal pivots. **Completion criterion:** initial compromise assessment, exposure-history-based lookback, retention limits and escalation of positive findings — recommended target October 23, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** A fixed GlobalProtect gateway still needs a prior-access review if it was exposed while vulnerable.

### Signal 3 — [Horizon 1] ConnectWise application abuse demands tenant-level containment
**Assessment:** Microsoft attributes ConnectWise Cloud Backup downstream abuse to Storm-0940, according to CyberScoop. Compromised application credentials enabled access beyond interactive MFA, and added credentials could survive disabling the original application. Potentially affected tenants need independent review before connections resume.

**Confidence:** High — substantive reporting quotes Microsoft, ConnectWise and investigators; attribution is Microsoft’s assessment, and total compromised tenants remain unresolved.

**What happened:** October 20 reporting describes unauthorized application sign-ins and additional application credentials used for persistence. On October 21, Microsoft attributed the campaign and reported agent-assisted follow-on directory operations. ConnectWise began phased restoration but advised customers to keep connections disabled. Its vendor-side observation of no successful activity since mitigations does not establish individual tenant safety. [CyberScoop, 2026-10-20](https://cyberscoop.com/connectwise-cloud-backup-supply-chain-attack/), [CyberScoop, 2026-10-21](https://cyberscoop.com/microsoft-attributes-connectwise-supply-chain-attack-china-storm-0940/).

**Defender impact:** Entra service-principal sign-ins, application credentials, grants and privileged-role changes—not only user sign-ins—are central investigation records.

**Relevance:** Matches supply-chain, nation-state and MFA-bypass interests; local use and granted permissions are unknown.

**Recommended actions:**

- **Act now:** Identity security — verify ConnectWise Cloud Backup application identities and grants this shift; if present, disable affected connections regardless of visible anomalies, preserving configuration evidence. **Completion criterion:** tenant applicability and disabled-state evidence, or documented absence — recommended target October 21, 2026.
- Incident response — preserve tenant audit and sign-in records this shift; retrieve verified indicators through the cited reporting and investigate added credentials, grants, roles and downstream access. **Completion criterion:** initial findings, persistence-removal scope and exposure-history/retention limits; successful authentication alone must not be recorded as proven theft — recommended target October 23, 2026.
- SaaS operations — prepare conditional reconnection readiness for affected tenants. **Dependencies:** vendor recovery guidance, Identity security containment and Incident response clearance. **Completion criterion:** named recovery owner, validated credential/grant state, backup-service validation plan and feasible restoration target; retain disabled connections until prerequisites are met — recommended target October 23, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** Vendor restoration is not tenant clearance when attackers may have created independent application credentials.

### Signal 4 — [Horizon 1] LiteLLM release compromise exposes execution environments
**Assessment:** The Register reports malicious LiteLLM release artifacts capable of credential theft and remote execution. If affected artifacts ran, removing the dependency alone is insufficient: contain execution environments and assess every credential accessible to them.

**Confidence:** Moderate — detailed secondary reporting attributes technical findings to several researchers; release-process root cause and affected population remain unresolved.

**What happened:** The reported malicious release is `1.107.0`, distributed through PyPI and container registries; mutable tags included `latest`, `main-latest` and `main-stable`. Python startup files reportedly execute the stealer and remote-access payload. Researchers identify `/tmp/.pc_once_*` and `/tmp/remote_code_loader.lock` as positive execution artifacts; their absence does not prove non-execution. The report names `1.106.2` as the most recent safe release. [The Register, 2026-10-21](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/10/21/litellm-supply-chain-attack-hoovers-up-passwords-and-secrets/5304548).

**Defender impact:** CI runners and proxy containers may expose cloud, model-provider and developer credentials beyond the package’s intended function.

**Relevance:** Direct supply-chain match; local installation, artifact digests and execution history are unknown.

**Recommended actions:**

- **Act now:** Application security — check package locks, image digests and deployment history this shift for `1.107.0` and implicated mutable tags; stop affected deployments and isolate execution environments while preserving evidence. **Completion criterion:** affected/absent/unknown classification per environment and verified replacement-artifact provenance — recommended target October 22, 2026.
- Incident response — investigate affected Python execution and enumerate accessible secrets; initiate revocation of exposed credentials through their owners. **Completion criterion:** execution findings, credential-response scope and a clean-rebuild plan with recovery owner and dependencies; keep restoration open pending validation — recommended target October 23, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** Treat execution of the compromised LiteLLM artifact as a host-and-credentials incident, not just a dependency rollback.

### Signal 5 — [Horizon 1] NetScaler persistence survives appliance reboot workflows
**Assessment:** Rapid7 documents a NetScaler intrusion where chained vulnerabilities enabled root execution and persistence across reboot and high-availability workflows. If affected appliances are deployed, review the pair and compromise state rather than treating reboot or patch installation as clearance.

**Confidence:** High — direct investigation correlates logs and filesystem evidence; the report describes one investigated intrusion, not campaign prevalence.

**What happened:** Rapid7 links CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88779 to log poisoning, a SAML crash condition and post-reboot root execution on an affected `14.1` build. Observed activity included web shells, tunneling, reconnaissance and configuration/key-material exfiltration. Both identifiers are KEV-listed. [Rapid7, 2026-10-19](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ra-netscaler-intrusions-chaining-cve-2026-88771-and-cve-2026-88779), [CISA KEV catalog, date unavailable](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

**Defender impact:** Crash-handler activity and HA synchronization become investigation surfaces; appliance configuration and key theft can require recovery beyond software updates.

**Relevance:** Direct Citrix match; deployment, SAML configuration and remediation status remain unknown.

**Recommended actions:**

- **Act now:** Infrastructure — inventory NetScaler pairs for CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88779 this shift; retrieve applicable Citrix remediation guidance and contain affected exposure pending supported updates. **Completion criterion:** both-node applicability, tested remediation and documented exceptions — recommended target October 22, 2026.
- Incident response — preserve appliance evidence this shift and review crash/reboot sequences, web shells, persistence and configuration access against Rapid7’s report. **Completion criterion:** initial findings and conditional recovery plan covering both nodes and exposed key material, with vendor prerequisites and restoration target unresolved until validated — recommended target October 23, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** Review both NetScaler nodes for persistence; a reboot is not evidence of recovery.

### Signal 6 — [Horizon 2] Compromised intermediates require non-browser trust review
**Assessment:** Browser blocking does not establish protection for every TLS client against compromised eMudhra intermediate keys. Review separately managed trust stores and embedded runtimes, prioritizing software that retrieves sensitive data or build dependencies.

**Confidence:** High — Talos provides certificate identities and runtime remediation details; local trust behavior and malicious use remain unverified.

**What happened:** Talos reports eight compromised intermediate certificates: six for TLS and two for code signing. It reports browser-vendor blocking and Microsoft code-signing blocking, while Go fixes for CVE-2026-111943 are available in `1.27.3` and `1.26.10`. Talos had not observed malicious incidents as of its stated October 21 observation. [Cisco Talos, 2026-10-21](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/compromised-intermediate-certificates/).

**Defender impact:** Revocation behavior varies across applications; interception additionally requires a suitable network position, and fraudulent TLS does not bypass independent package-integrity checks.

**Recommended actions:**

- Security engineering — begin a trust-path review within 72 hours for Go services, VPN software and independently managed CA stores; compare certificate identities against Talos and retrieve product-specific fixes. **Completion criterion:** tested rejection or verified update evidence, plus owned exceptions and vendor dependencies — recommended target October 28, 2026.

**Decision window:** 72 hours

**The line:** Confirm distrust in the clients that matter; browser updates do not validate every application’s trust path.

---

## DEVELOPING SITUATIONS

### GitLab fix coverage needs authoritative mapping
**Trajectory:** Uncertain — October 22 reporting, published within this Chicago edition day, says October 21 fixes expand coverage beyond the October 12 update. Exact fixed versions are absent from the retained passage. [The Hacker News, 2026-10-22](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/critical-gitlab-flaw-cvss-100-could.html).

**Watch criteria:** Escalate when the vendor advisory establishes exact affected/fixed versions. Application security should retrieve it and check self-managed inventory by recommended target October 22, 2026; an earlier patch ticket is not sufficient applicability evidence.

---

## CONVERGENCE

No supported intersection is established by the current retained evidence.

---

## WATCHLIST — THROUGH October 24, 2026

- **Plex:** Infrastructure confirms absence or updates affected installations to `1.43.3.10861` or later after verifying vendor guidance. Reports describe four chained KEV vulnerabilities, not a consumer-only risk exemption. CVE-2026-96654: CISA FCEB remediation due October 23, 2026; CVE-2026-96656: CISA FCEB remediation due October 23, 2026. [CISA Advisories, 2026-10-20](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/10/20/cisa-adds-six-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog), [BleepingComputer, 2026-10-21](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-hackers-chain-plex-flaws-in-plex2shell-attacks-to-breach-servers/), [The Hacker News, 2026-10-21](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/cisa-orders-federal-agencies-to-patch.html).
- **Siemens Software Center:** Endpoint engineering verifies absence or rollout of `4.0.9.8` or later for exploited CVE-2026-110936; the product name alone does not establish ICS exposure. [CCCS, 2026-10-20](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/siemens-security-advisory-av26-1063).
- **SiteGuard:** Infrastructure verifies affected deployments and vendor-supported upgrades for CVE-2026-106931. CISA FCEB remediation due October 23, 2026; local completion requires its own applicability and change decision. [BleepingComputer, 2026-10-21](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-hackers-chain-plex-flaws-in-plex2shell-attacks-to-breach-servers/), [CISA KEV catalog, date unavailable](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).
- **Gitea:** Application security retrieves per-identifier fix guidance and records applicability for CVE-2026-20896 and KEV-listed CVE-2026-60004; CCCS reports exploitation of the former without establishing identical scope for both. [CCCS, 2026-10-20](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/gitea-security-advisory-av26-845).
- **BeyondTrust:** Infrastructure verifies `BT26-05-RS` installation or absence of affected Remote Support deployments; Incident response opens prior-compromise review where applicable. Older unsupported patch targets require upgrade first. [Rapid7, 2026-10-19](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-102764-critical-beyondtrust-remote-support-authentication-bypass-exploited-in-the-wild).
- **Vulnerability prioritization:** Vulnerability management records whether internet reachability and authentication requirements influence emergency triage. Rapid7’s Q3 findings concern its tracked exploited vulnerabilities, not a universal three-day remediation guarantee. [Rapid7, 2026-10-21](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/tr-q3-2026-threat-update-attackers-exploiting-vulnerabilities-within-3-days), [SecurityWeek, 2026-10-21](https://www.securityweek.com/high-severity-flaws-exploited-in-three-days-as-ransomware-dominates-q3-rapid7/).
- **PAN-OS embedded PHP:** Infrastructure verifies management-web-interface restrictions while vendor fixes remain pending in the October 21 advisory; GlobalProtect portal and gateway are explicitly outside this separate PHP issue. [Palo Alto Security Advisories, 2026-10-21](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618).

sources.title: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20)
sources.passage: Threat Research Center High Profile Threats Vulnerabilities Vulnerabilities Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20) 5 min read Related Products Advanced URL Filtering Cortex Cortex Xpanse GlobalProtect Next-Generation Firewall Unit 42 Deep and Dark Web Service Unit 42 Incident Response Unit 42 Threat Intelligence Services By: Andy Piazza Unit 42 Published: October 20, 2026 Categories: High Profile Threats Vulnerabilities Tags: CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerability Share Executive Summary October 19 Update: Unit 42 continues to observe attempted exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 by ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka Inc). We’re also aware of public reporting attributing exploitation to threat actors using Settra ransomware. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has observed active exploitation of PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 by an unidentified threat actor attempting to access GlobalProtect. This security flaw involves an authentication bypass in the portal and gateway components of vulnerable versions of PAN-OS ® software, which could allow unauthorized attackers to circumvent security controls and initiate virtual private network (VPN) connections. […] We advise organizations to proactively hunt for the indicators of the activity specified in this report and activate incident response protocols for any successful gateway-connected events linked to these indicators. Additionally, we strongly recommend reviewing the security advisory for CVE-2026-0257 , following the available workarounds and mitigations or upgrading to a version that includes a fix for this issue. […] Management Interface Exposure Risk and Remediation During incident response (IR) engagements associated with the Lunar Peak campaign , Unit 42 observed a recurring misconfiguration that led to critical, unintended exposure. […] Verification and mitigation: Verify exposure : Defenders can rapidly verify whether their environments are affected by attempting an out-of-band HTTPS connection to their management IP address on ports 4443 and 3879 via an external web browser. Remediate : To remediate this issue and enforce the principle of least privilege, we strongly advise administrators to review official Palo Alto Networks documentation on configuring Interface Management profiles to safely restrict access. […] Following this, the threat actors are typically: Conducting internal network reconnaissance using dual-use remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools Moving laterally via RDP and SMB Staging additional tooling for credential harvesting, data exfiltration and ultimately, ransomware deployment Our investigations have been ongoing since early June 2026 and have spanned across numerous industries, including: Education Financial services Healthcare High technology Hospitality Manufacturing Professional and legal services Government Transportation and logistics Utilities and energy Wholesale and retail The most significant evolution in tactics, techniques and procedures (TTPs) following successful exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 is the direct pivot to the virtualization layer. In one notable case, attackers moved from the compromised VPN gateway to the vCenter management appliance. […] PT to add verification and remediation guidance. […]

sources.title: CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
sources.passage: Alert CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog Release Date October 20, 2026 CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-96652 Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability CVE-2026-96654 Plex Media Server Improper Neutralization of Encoded URI Schemes in a Web Page Vulnerability CVE-2026-96655 Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability CVE-2026-96656 Plex Media Server External Control of File Name or Path Vulnerability CVE-2026-106931 EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition OS Command Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-110936 Siemens Software Center Uncontrolled Search Path Element Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance. This product is provided subject to this Notification and this Privacy & Use policy. Please share your thoughts We recently updated our anonymous product survey ; we welcome your feedback.

sources.title: CISA: Hackers chain Plex flaws in Plex2Shell attacks to breach servers
sources.passage: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server. The security issues are collectively called Plex2Shell. When chained in an exploit, an attacker can obtain the owner's admin token and execute code with elevated privileges. Plex Media Server is a popular media suite that helps users organize personal collections of movies, TV shows, music, and photos, and stream them to other devices at home or remotely over the internet. CISA has directed federal agencies to prioritize patching systems affected by Plex2Shell vulnerabilities or apply mitigations by October 23. The security issues were discovered by security researcher Zach Main, who reported them responsibly to Plex on July 27. The individual flaws are rated medium to high in severity, but the researcher assigns the full exploit chain a critical score of 9.8. CVE-2026-96652 – An SSRF flaw in /player/timeline that allows unauthenticated attackers to make Plex send POST requests to arbitrary destinations, including its own internal APIs. CVE-2026-96654 – A URL injection flaw in searchOne that allows attackers to invoke other plugins’ functions with attacker-controlled parameters. CVE-2026-96655 – An authenticated SSRF flaw in the transcoder endpoint that allows users to make Plex request arbitrary internal or external addresses. CVE-2026-96656 – An arbitrary file write flaw in the transcoder settings that allows administrators to plant malicious shared libraries that Plex subsequently loads, leading to code execution. Zach Main published full technical details for the Plex2Shell vulnerabilities on October 16, followed by a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit three days later. On October 17, reports of Plex2Shell being exploited in the wild started to emerge, intially targeting Plex honeypots to deploy a cryptominer. Plex2Shell impacts Plex Media Server versions before 1.43.3.10861, which was released on August 4 . Hackers also target Siemens Software Center Alongside Plex2Shell, CISA has added to its catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) an uncontrolled search path element flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110936, in Siemens Software Center (SSC). The German technology giant warned on October 19 that hackers were leveraging the vulnerability in campaigns linked to a multi-payload ClickFix delivery platform called Romulus. Recent research from operational technology (OT) cybersecurity company Forescout notes that Romulus "may be a privately operated panel, a commercial cybercriminal delivery service, an affiliate framework, or software that has been copied between operators." Siemens's alert on CVE-2026-110936 shares indicators of compromise (IoCs) and advice on identifying compromised systems, urging administrators to update Siemens Software Center to version 4.0.9.8 or later. CISA has also added CVE-2026-106931 to KEV, an OS command injection flaw that affects affecting the SiteGuard Server Edition web application firewall (WAF). Both the vendor and Japan's CERT flagged CVE-2026-106931 as actively exploited late last week. The vendor urged users to upgrade to SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd, Nginx, and IIS version 8.00 Update 5, and SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd and Nginx on FreeBSD version 7.00 Update 6 and later. Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply. sources.title: CISA Orders Federal Agencies to Patch Exploited Plex2Shell, Siemens, and SiteGuard Flaws
sources.passage: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog, including four vulnerabilities impacting Plex Media Server that's collectively called Plex2Shell . The vulnerabilities are listed below - CVE-2026-96652 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability CVE-2026-96654 (CVSS score: 6.9) - Plex Media Server improper neutralization of encoded URI schemes in a web page Vulnerability CVE-2026-96655 (CVSS score: 5.3) - Plex Media Server Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability CVE-2026-96656 (CVSS score: 8.6) - Plex Media Server external control of file name or path Vulnerability According to security researcher Zach Main, who discovered and reported the vulnerabilities, a remote attacker could chain the four vulnerabilities to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The issues were addressed in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 released on August 3, 2026. The addition of the four vulnerabilities to the KEV catalog follows a report from security researcher boredhackerblog, who found that threat actors are weaponizing the flaws to deploy cryptocurrency miners and proxy malware. CISA has also flagged two other vulnerabilities as actively exploited. One of them is a DLL sideloading vulnerability in Siemens Software Center ( CVE-2026-110936 , CVSS score: 8.4) that has been abused in ClickFix attacks using a platform called Romulus. The second security flaw is a command injection bug in EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition ( CVE-2026-106931 , CVSS score: 8.5) that the Japanese company confirmed as being exploited. No additional details related to the exploitation activity are currently available. CISA is urging Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to apply fixes for CVE-2026-106931, CVE-2026-96656, and CVE-2026-96654 by October 23, 2026, and the rest by November 3, 2026. sources.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
sources.passage: Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild. Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin. The flaws at issue are present in PHP, the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal, Magento, Joomla and WordPress. Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server. Reuters reports that government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline today after the PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed. Cloudflare said it has already detected some exploitation of the flaw, and that at 3:02 am (UTC) it implemented web application firewall rules to protect websites from attack traffic seeking to exploit the bugs, which could cause a denial of service condition, remote code execution, and data exposure. OpenAI, which was involved in the vulnerability research and outreach, said “given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.” Censys, a company that tracks the technology used by Internet hosts, said a recent scan identified approximately 2.58 million Internet facing hosts and 54.9 million web properties running PHP. Security experts at Wiz said every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities [full disclosure: Wiz is an advertiser on this blog]. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” reads a blog post published today by a team of researchers at Wiz, which was one of several organizations credited with discovering the vulnerabilities. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.” The Wiz researchers say it is likely the PHP vulnerabilities will be mass-exploited to install web-based backdoors or “web shells,” which give attackers a web-based panel that allows them to remotely control infected sites. Wiz said that prior to the PHP bugs being publicly disclosed, the company worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI to measure the size of the problem and coordinate patch verification and disclosure. The PHP zero-day vulnerabilities are being tracked by their CVE numbers, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and they affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later. The bugs are fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. According to Wiz, PHP is so deeply embedded in many web applications that we are likely to see organizations struggling to patch these vulnerabilities for some time to come, comparing this PHP vulnerability pair with the Log4Shell weakness that emerged in 2021 — a widespread, severe-as-it-gets security flaw in Log4j, a popular Java logging framework. “A vulnerability in core PHP reaches far beyond a single application,” the Wiz researchers wrote. “PHP runs across clouds, hosting providers, content-delivery networks and millions of independently managed servers. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem.” The SANS Internet Storm Center is keeping an eye on major software platforms that are shipping updates to deal with these PHP flaws. For example, Ubuntu just released updated PHP packages. For a technical deep-dive on these vulnerabilities that tells the timeline of the discovery of these bugs in a comic book style, check out this post from Calif, another technology company credited with finding the PHP flaws. This is a fast-moving story. Updates will be noted here with timestamps. Update, 2:30 pm ET: Add figures from Censys and a link to Calif’s writeup.

sources.title: High-Severity Flaws Exploited in Three Days as Ransomware Dominates Q3: Rapid7
sources.passage: High-severity flaws are exploited faster; ransomware remains the dominant threat; the US is the world’s most targeted country, and attacks increasingly involve the use of AI (but largely manually rather than autonomously). Rapid7’s threat analysis for Q3, 2026 adds color to these basic details of the current threat landscape. […] That’s interesting because the board-deck version of this year has been wall-to-wall AI attackers, and the data doesn’t support that story,” Douglas McKee, director of vulnerability intelligence at Rapid7 told SecurityWeek . […] What is growing, however, is automation of the ‘tactical middle’ of the attack chain: technique selection, target triage, and recovering from a failed step can all now run without a human being present.
